Trump’s campaign against the media continues to escalate.

The latest move targets another major news organization as the Trump administration increases pressure on media outlets that have engaged in years of biased, misleading, or politically motivated reporting. According to the report, the administration views this as part of a broader effort to hold legacy media accountable through legal challenges, regulatory scrutiny, and public pressure.

This isn’t happening in isolation. Since returning to office, Trump has pursued lawsuits against news organizations, challenged press access in certain circumstances, scrutinized federally funded broadcasters, and repeatedly called out major media outlets for spreading misinformation, interfering in elections, and operating as political actors rather than neutral journalists.

There is also an interesting historical parallel. During the Civil War, President Abraham Lincoln’s administration took extraordinary actions against parts of the press, including the arrest or detention of some newspaper editors and publishers accused of undermining the Union war effort or publishing information viewed as harmful to national security.

The current effort is about restoring accountability to institutions that have abused the public’s trust. 

 If tensions between the administration and legacy media continue to escalate, the historical comparison to periods of heightened conflict between the government and the press may become even more relevant.
